citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
The written narrative description of the methods and sources used to determine that alternatives were not available in
Protocol #25-025 did not illustrate that the principal investigator considered alternatives to the aortic constriction
procedure described in the protocol. This procedure causes more than momentary pain and/or distress. Proposals to
conduct an animal activity must contain enough detail for the IACUC to determine that proposed activities or significant
changes in ongoing activities meet all requirements as outlined in Part 2, Subpart C, Section 2.31(d). Details are to
include the consideration of alternatives when there is a possibility of causing more than momentary or slight pain or
distress to the animals, and a written narrative description of the methods and sources used to determine that alternatives
were not available. The protocol did not contain all the needed information for the IACUC to properly assess if/how pain
and distress could be limited to that which is unavoidable for the conduct of scientifically valuable research.
The IACUC shall determine that the principal investigator has both considered alternatives to procedures that may cause
more than momentary or slight pain or distress to the animals and provided a written narrative description of the methods
and sources used to determine that alternatives were not available.
Correct by August 17, 2026.

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
On April 14, 2026, the IACUC voted to suspend “all aortic constriction surgeries” in Protocol #25-025. The Institutional
Official, however, did not report the suspended protocol activity to APHIS or the Federal agency funding the activity along
with a full explanation of the reasons for the suspension and the corrective action as required by this Section. Failure to
report suspension actions to APHIS (and any other Federal agency funding that activity) prevents Federal oversight and
tracking of animal welfare concerns.
The Institutional Official shall notify APHIS and any Federal agency funding that activity of the suspension along with a full
explanation of the corrective actions to be taken.
Correct by July 17, 2026.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
The research facility did not have appropriate equipment to provide adequate veterinary care. According to IACUC
records and to facility representatives, on March 25, 2026, three animals underwent aortic constriction surgery on
Protocol #25-025; however, one of the animals (1416) did not recover after surgery, failing to breathe on their own after
being taken off the ventilator. On March 26, 2026, three additional animals underwent aortic constriction surgery;
however, two of the animals (1418, 1419) experienced respiratory distress resulting in the need for the animals to be
humanely euthanized. The IACUC attributed the animal deaths to unreliable ventilator function during the surgical
procedures.
Procedures performed on animals requiring ventilation must be conducted utilizing properly calibrated and maintained
equipment.
Each research facility shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include availability of
appropriate equipment, among other requirements, to comply with the provisions of this subchapter.
Correct prior to procedures requiring use of a ventilator.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
